newsitem.title: USA: ITT plan marks end of leftover conglomerate.
newsitem.headline: ITT plan marks end of leftover conglomerate.

text.p: A plan by ITT Corp. to split into three companies marks the death of a huge conglomerate that once sold everything from Twinkies to telephones.

Even after a spinoff in 1995 that broke off the company's industrial and insurance businesses, ITT was loaded with unrelated parts, including a prized casino and hotel business, a stake in a French telecommunications firm and a group of technical schools.
The structure caused problems for investors and analysts when they tried to evaluate the disparate operations.

"I'm happy to get the noise out of the way. It was just extra steps to go through. Investors like clarity and predictibility," said Prudential Securities analyst Joseph Coccimiglio, who follows the company.

The restructuring announced Wednesday calls for ITT to break into three more companies. The casino and hotel business will be called ITT Destinations Inc., a telephone directories business will continue as ITT Corp. and the trade schools unit -- previously an 83.3 percent-owned subsidiary -- will be known as ITT Educational Services Inc.

Although the plan is widely considered ITT's latest effort to prevent a $6.5 billion hostile takeover attempt by Hilton Hotels Corp., ITT insists it has always wanted to separate the non-casino and lodging businesses.

"The educational services and world directories businesses didn't fit anyplace," said spokesman Jim Gallagher, referring to the company's 1995 split. "We knew then that we didn't want them as part of the long-term scheme of this company."
ITT has sold non-core assets in recent months in an effort to thwart a Hilton takeover, including the stake in Alacatel Alsthom and its 50 percent ownership of Madison Square Garden.

Chairman Rand Araskog, who started selling parts of ITT shortly after taking over its helm in 1979, is hoping the break-up will bring more attention to the parts that have been overshadowed by high-profile Caesars World and Sheraton. Most notably, the world telephone directories business is a highly profitable operation with strong prospects for expansion.

"The new separation will create three highly focused companies with excellent prospects. We expect enhanced reserach coverage and institutional investor interest in each of these businesses because the companies will now be easier to understand and they each will have meaningful public floats and trading liquidity," Araskog told analysts in a conference call on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, ITT also has launched a pre-emptive strike against Beverly Hills, Calif.-based Hilton to stop it from trying to block the plan. On Wednesday, ITT filed papers in U.S. District Court in Las Vegas seeking a ruling that it has the right to pursue the breakup.
"It would be illogical if the board could not pursue the plan now, particularly given the threats to ITT posed by the Hilton bid," ITT said in court papers.

Hilton, which has lost several court fights aimed at forcing the takeover to move forward, has blasted the plan and vowed to pursue legal options. A Hilton spokesman declined to comment on ITT's court filing.
In the court filing, ITT contends that Hilton cannot show the plan violates Nevada law or that ITT's board acted outside of its power by approving the plan.
"Despite the merits of the plan, Hilton's litigation record to date makes it highly likely that Hilton will seek to challenge the plan," ITT said.
ITT fell $1.375 to $65.56 Thursday on the New York Stock Exchange. Hilton slipped 37.5 cents to $28.94, also on the NYSE.
